premise.displayText: The Restroom Key Nobody Could Steal

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Legally Brent
jokes.joke: I ordered a coffee, and the barista asked my name. I said, “Ben.” She confidently wrote “Brent” without hesitation. That level of certainty changed me. I spent the rest of the day introducing myself as Brent. If a woman with an apron and a Sharpie can rebrand you before 9 a.m., apparently that’s legally binding.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Oat Milk Revenge
jokes.joke: I worked as a barista for two years, and it made me a genuinely vindictive person. Somebody corrects my name spelling now, I don't get mad, I get creative. You said your name's 'Kyle, with a Y'? Cool. Enjoy your scalding oat milk, 'Kyle with a Y,' written on the cup in cursive, ready in forty-five minutes, at a Starbucks across town that you don't even remember walking into.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Restroom Key
jokes.joke: I had to ask the gas station clerk for the bathroom key, and he handed me a rusty brass key chained to a full-sized snow shovel so nobody steals it. Ten minutes later, I had to walk back up to the counter and admit I lost the shovel.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Tip Adjustment
jokes.joke: I shorted a barista on the tip last week. Next time I ordered my usual triple espresso. She handed it over with a big smile. I downed the whole thing and felt nothing—pure decaf. Then she leaned in and said, 'Sleep tight.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Fuel Crisis
jokes.joke: I once lost my wallet at a gas station and tried to stay calm, but you can’t look confident while patting yourself down like you’re checking for spare organs. The cashier asked if everything was okay, and I said, “Yeah, just deciding which limb to sell so I can get home.”

scores.comment: Clear vindictive-barista premise with decent escalation, but the final across-town image feels overextended rather than sharply punched.
Excellent compact construction: concrete setup, strong visual absurdity, and a clean reversal when the supposedly unlosable object is lost.
Clean and economical with a proper final tag, but decaf as barista revenge is fairly foreseeable and limits the surprise.
The spare-organs image is amusing, but the limb-selling tag is more familiar; it also clearly introduces confidence as a third seed concept.
Clean setup and escalation with a solid closing line, but the 'rebranding' angle is a fairly familiar comic shape.
Vivid, absurd image (shovel-chained key) with a clean escalation and a punchline that actually pays off the setup.
Decent revenge premise, but the decaf logic and 'sleep tight' close land a bit murky rather than snapping clearly.
Strong physical comedy with the organ-patting image and a punchy, well-timed closing line.
Solid stage cadence and a clear progression, though the 'Starbucks spelled my name wrong' setup is well-worn territory.
Overstuffed escalation that dissolves into surreal rambling rather than snapping to a crisp, punchy finish.
Clean economy and effective misdirection with the decaf switch, anchored by a tight, spoken final tag.
Relatable physical image during the pat-down, but the scripted dialogue punchline lands soft.
Clean name-misspell premise with mild rebranding payoff; pleasant but low-stakes.
Strong vindictive escalation with vivid multi-layer revenge; lands cleanly.
Tight visual setup and inevitable admission punch; excellent stage economy.
Generic lost-wallet panic; limb line feels forced and under-delivers.
Clean premise with a confident rebranding turn; mildly funny and well-timed.
Strong voice and escalation; the vindictive twist lands a modest real laugh.
Funny visual and a sharp final admission; genuinely good timing and turn.
Decaf revenge is a familiar angle but executed cleanly with a solid closer.
